findings.title: C++ reset tail ends before post-reset read
findings.baselineFact: transferTestPayload sends 1B/O then full 1A write and returns true. sendUsbCommand(replyLength=0) never invokes a read. The later Python lifecycle fix does not alter this C++ path.
findings.recommendation: Use the injected engine to retain commitAccepted/resetWritten and require the already observed post-reset read return before releasing ownership. Do not require a new reset ACK; accept -5 only after the matched AMT start/all segments/commit/reset sequence.

findings.title: Boolean result discards commit uncertainty
findings.baselineFact: writeUsbBytes/readUsbReply retain only one localized QString; transferTestPayload combines commit/reset using &&. A fully written 1B with bad/missing ACK and an accepted commit followed by short reset both return false without structured distinctions. CLI emits only ok/message and exit 14 for every transfer failure.
findings.recommendation: Retain the first failure plus all milestones and written/acknowledged segment names. Fully written 1B without valid ACK is commit_status_unknown; commit ACK with reset failure is committed_reset_not_written. Do not auto-retry or claim rollback.

findings.title: Start-option bytes differ between legacy C++ and later native verification
findings.baselineFact: Active legacy C++ sends 34 options 010101. The later native lifecycle classifier accepts 000000 for runs with all four clear/update UI fields false. The old phase6 plan still documents 010101 and says full parameter semantics remain unknown.
findings.recommendation: Record actual option bytes in contract/result. Root has selected the observed 000000 product default, with 010101 retained only as an explicit legacy choice. Permit these two observed values only; do not invent names or semantics for unproven individual bits.

findings.title: No injectable seam or I/O fault tests in current plan target
findings.baselineFact: UsbFunctions is private and Q_OS_WIN-only inside the compiler-heavy independent_downloader.cpp. KinSealDeviceTransferTests links only device_transfer_plan.cpp and checks ordering/framing, so it cannot exercise open/claim, partial writes, wrong ACK, timeouts, or reset completion.
findings.recommendation: Extract QtCore-only device_transfer_engine.h/.cpp accepting std::function callbacks for open/claim/write/read/release/close. Keep native discovery/library ownership in root adapter. Add app-less engine tests, with no driver loading or hardware discovery.

findings.title: UI owns one worker but has no actual cancellation transaction
findings.baselineFact: downloadToDevice stores a private KSP and hidden same-executable QProcess; its progress dialog has no cancel button. No cancellation signal/IPC or worker token is wired. Removing the button does not implement a cancel state machine.
findings.recommendation: Keep immutable input ownership. Add only an explicit cancellation protocol with safe sampling boundaries; allow no-write exit after open/claim and stop between segment data/status before commit. Once full commit frame is written, ignore cancellation until ACK/reset/read cleanup completes. Never label a started transfer rolled back.

findings.title: Duplicate-launch guard covers one MainWindow only
findings.baselineFact: m_downloadProcess is assigned before start, action_USBdownload is disabled for Starting/Running/finalization and finalize checks captured process identity. This is a useful existing guard. Separate GUI instances and independent CLI processes have no shared lock; USB discovery selects the first matching VID/PID.
findings.recommendation: Retain the existing local guard. Add an adapter-level named process/device lock before open, reject multiple matching devices or bind an explicit identity, and release the lock only after the worker exits/driver cleanup. A lock protects app instances, not unrelated vendor processes; claim errors must remain explicit.

findings.title: Parent close waits for owner but cannot recover a hung worker
findings.baselineFact: closeEvent ignores close while m_downloadProcess is non-null. QProcess finished/FailedToStart finalizes once, cleans temporary input and restores actions. There is no application-level worker deadline or cancel path. Other QProcess errors are only handled indirectly through finished; no streaming progress is parsed.
findings.recommendation: Preserve close refusal during active side effects. Introduce an owned session/controller for start, progress, cancellation request, finish, and cleanup; retain final result before deleting temporary input. A watchdog must report unknown device state instead of silently killing/retrying after commit. Tests should cover FailedToStart/crash/close/repeated completion without real QProcess USB execution.

findings.title: Acquisition and cleanup have weak diagnostics
findings.baselineFact: resolveUsbFunctions correctly loads system libusb0.dll and verifies symbols. downloadPreparedPayload opens first matching 7365:616C and claims interface 0; discovery return counts are ignored. release/close are called after transfer but their results are discarded.
findings.recommendation: Keep library/handle in the native adapter, inject every acquisition/cleanup call, retain opened/interfaceClaimed and release/close results, and preserve the original protocol error if cleanup fails. Do not issue release if claim failed; close every successful open.

findings.title: 24-byte identity checks are limited and fragmented reads are rejected
findings.baselineFact: readUsbReply asks for capacity32 for expected24, or capacity4 for expected1; it makes one read and accepts exact returned length plus first byte only. All remaining reply bytes are discarded. Its timeout is fixed10000ms per call, not a proved firmware maximum.
findings.recommendation: Preserve full short reply bytes and raw requested/returned values separately from expected reply length. Keep exact single-read rejection for this engine slice; retry/reassembly needs separate protocol evidence. Retain firmware identity as unverified beyond existing first-byte scope.

findings.title: Plan length bound is checked before the additional upload wire prefix
findings.baselineFact: buildDeviceTransferPlan rejects payload sizes above INT_MAX but appends four more bytes to upLoad.knr. An original upload block at the signed driver size limit would produce an oversized wire buffer; this is a theoretical bound issue, not a demonstrated supported-project failure.
findings.recommendation: Check upload source size <= INT_MAX-4 before building the framed plan, and check all final wire lengths/options before any open. Do not allocate gigabytes solely to test this bound.

findings.title: Compile-first and immutable snapshot safeguards already exist
findings.baselineFact: downloadProject builds all supported compiler payloads before downloadPreparedPayload. The latter builds a valid transfer plan before driver resolution/open. UI cancels in-flight canvas interaction and saves a private KSP, so later editor changes do not change this worker input.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these safeguards and do not move compile or plan validation behind device open. Do not claim unsupported controls/multipage are enabled by the transport engine.

findings.title: Plan fixtures prove ordering, not real ACK/firmware behavior
findings.baselineFact: The four existing slots cover static, dynamic and macro plan order and incomplete input preserving the previous plan. Macro host-order evidence is explicitly not a hardware ACK claim. Stage2 workflow test only checks download action re-enables when a document reopens.
findings.recommendation: Reuse all four plan slots unchanged. Add engine fault tests and separate controller tests. Keep real USB T and screen/PLC E as independent later acceptance.
